title: Georgia Tech / GTRI Research Bridge

audience.name: Georgia Tech / Georgia Tech Research Institute

hero.headline: Test the representation. Keep the null result.
hero.support: This unlisted brief proposes a small research-engineering collaboration: make one representation explicit, compare it with a strong baseline, preserve negative results, and let the evidence determine whether the added structure is useful.

whyThisBridge: The founder has prior Georgia Tech research experience in computer architecture and high-performance computing, which makes rigorous experimental comparison a natural point of contact.
The current BFL work includes formalization, benchmark construction, computational experiments, provenance recovery, and deliberate attempts to reduce new language to established methods.
The ask is not institutional validation of Boundary First Labs. It is independent technical criticism of one bounded research object.
candidateWork: Recover and narrow the historical NUMA experiment into an inspectable technical note whose claim remains tied to the actual workload and hardware regime.
Build a bounded Schemathematics typed-graph prototype and benchmark structured mathematical navigation against ordinary semantic retrieval.
Test representation choice through null, baseline, equivalence, transport, composition, provenance, limit, and counterexample tests.
Develop one research-engineering case where an apparently meaningful structural distinction fails to improve a measurable computational objective.
whatBFLBrings: Research-engineering and software architecture experience across ambiguous domains.
Schemathematics, Representational Mechanics, Admissibility, and distinction-space research programs.
A claim discipline that preserves negative results and retires unnecessary abstractions.
Prototype and workbench capability for turning formal hypotheses into inspectable computational artifacts.
whatTheInstitutionCouldBring: Relevant expertise in computing, systems, modeling, formal methods, or applied research engineering.
A benchmark environment or bounded problem where representation choice is consequential.
firstAsk: Review one bounded research object: tell us what the existing field already explains, what—if anything—the proposed representation adds, and what experiment would falsify that added layer.
claimBoundary: This page does not imply Georgia Tech or GTRI endorsement, affiliation, sponsorship, or active collaboration.
Historical founder research participation must remain scoped as contributing work inside an existing research direction.
The precise historical NUMA performance claim remains unpublished until supporting experiment artifacts are recovered and independently checked.
A successful collaboration would validate only the bounded result studied, not Boundary Theory as a whole.
